Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Siding FAQ

When should damaged siding be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be recommended when damage is widespread, materials are deteriorated, moisture has reached the sheathing or matching repairs would not provide a durable and consistent result.

Can siding damage lead to water intrusion?

Yes. Open joints, cracks, missing panels, failed caulking and damaged trim can allow moisture behind the exterior finish and should be evaluated promptly.

Can you repair soffit, fascia and exterior trim with the siding project?

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

Do siding repairs include painting and sealing?

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Bathroom Remodeling • Bedford, Texas

Bathroom Ventilation Improvements in Bedford, TX

Bathroom ventilation helps remove moisture when the fan is correctly sized, ducted and used long enough.

Bathroom ventilation site checklist

  • Room dimensions, ceiling height and shower enclosure
  • Fan label, condition, controls and observed airflow
  • Duct diameter, length, bends and insulation where accessible
  • Outdoor termination and working backdraft damper
  • Peeling paint, staining, soft drywall or recurring condensation

Start with the moisture pattern

A replacement fan should be selected after documenting the room and how moisture behaves. Persistent condensation may reflect low airflow, a restricted duct, short run time or another moisture source, so the inspection should not assume the fan is the only problem.

Check the complete air path

The grille, fan housing, duct connections and exterior hood work as one system. Accessible sections should be checked for crushed duct, excessive bends and disconnections. The room also needs a path for replacement air when the door is closed.

Sequence finish repairs correctly

Roof or plumbing leaks must be corrected separately. Damaged areas should be evaluated and ready for reconstruction before new drywall, primer or bathroom paint is installed, reducing the chance that a fresh finish hides an unresolved condition.

Bathroom Waterproofing Details in Frisco, TX

Waterproofing must form a continuous system behind tile, around penetrations and across changes of plane.

Waterproofing scope checklist

  • Demolition limits and condition of framing or subfloor
  • Drain location and finished slope to the drain
  • Compatible pan, wall-board and membrane components
  • Seams, corners, curbs, niches and plumbing penetrations
  • Inspection or water-test requirements for the selected assembly

Treat waterproofing as a complete assembly

Tile and grout are finish surfaces, not the entire water-management system. The drain, sloped base, wall substrate, membrane, seams and penetrations must be planned together using components approved for the selected installation method.

Inspect what demolition reveals

Previous leaks, movement, swollen subfloor or out-of-square framing can change the scope. Those conditions should be documented before covering the walls so repair decisions and any concealed-condition changes remain clear.

Verify before tile conceals the work

Required inspections and testing depend on the assembly and local authority. The scope should identify who coordinates them and when tile may begin, while photographs preserve a record of corners, penetrations and other details that will no longer be visible.

Planning the work

Corners, niches, benches, curbs, valves and drain transitions deserve special attention because small gaps can create hidden damage.

Avoiding repeat problems

Flood testing or manufacturer-required checks should happen before finish materials cover the assembly.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Do you handle the complete bathroom project or only tile?

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Do you handle the complete bathroom project or only tile?

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Siding FAQ

When should damaged siding be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be recommended when damage is widespread, materials are deteriorated, moisture has reached the sheathing or matching repairs would not provide a durable and consistent result.

Can siding damage lead to water intrusion?

Yes. Open joints, cracks, missing panels, failed caulking and damaged trim can allow moisture behind the exterior finish and should be evaluated promptly.

Can you repair soffit, fascia and exterior trim with the siding project?

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

Do siding repairs include painting and sealing?

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Painting FAQ

What preparation is included before painting?

Preparation may include protecting floors and furnishings, cleaning surfaces, patching drywall, sanding, scraping loose coatings, caulking gaps and applying primer where needed.

When is primer necessary?

Primer is commonly recommended over new drywall, repairs, stains, bare wood, major color changes and surfaces where adhesion or sealing must be improved.

Do you paint occupied homes and active commercial spaces?

Yes. Work areas, access, ventilation and daily cleanup can be coordinated to reduce disruption while the property remains occupied or in operation.

Can exterior painting include siding, fascia, soffits and trim?

Yes. Exterior scopes can include siding, fascia, soffits, doors, trim and other approved surfaces after repairs and preparation are completed.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

How to Compare Contractor Estimates in Carrollton, TX

The lowest total is not always the lowest final cost when estimates describe different scopes, materials or exclusions.

  • Same rooms, measurements and demolition limits
  • Named materials, finish level and installation method
  • Allowances, exclusions and concealed-condition assumptions

Normalize the scope first

Two totals are not comparable when one includes demolition, disposal, preparation and finish repairs while another does not. Mark every included task and ask each contractor to clarify missing quantities or vague phrases.

Compare project controls

Review start conditions, estimated duration, payment milestones and who coordinates each trade. A written change-order process protects both parties by recording added work, price and schedule effects before the extra work proceeds.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

What preparation is included before painting?

Preparation may include protecting floors and furnishings, cleaning surfaces, patching drywall, sanding, scraping loose coatings, caulking gaps and applying primer where needed.

Primer is commonly recommended over new drywall, repairs, stains, bare wood, major color changes and surfaces where adhesion or sealing must be improved.

Yes. Work areas, access, ventilation and daily cleanup can be coordinated to reduce disruption while the property remains occupied or in operation.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Painting FAQ

What preparation is included before painting?

Preparation may include protecting floors and furnishings, cleaning surfaces, patching drywall, sanding, scraping loose coatings, caulking gaps and applying primer where needed.

When is primer necessary?

Coordinate the room edges

Preparation affects baseboards, cabinets, appliances, door clearance and adjacent floors. Recording finished heights and transition locations early reduces last-minute cuts and helps the new flooring continue cleanly through connected spaces.

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Siding FAQ

When should damaged siding be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be recommended when damage is widespread, materials are deteriorated, moisture has reached the sheathing or matching repairs would not provide a durable and consistent result.

Can siding damage lead to water intrusion?

Yes. Open joints, cracks, missing panels, failed caulking and damaged trim can allow moisture behind the exterior finish and should be evaluated promptly.

Can you repair soffit, fascia and exterior trim with the siding project?

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

Do siding repairs include painting and sealing?

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Siding FAQ

When should damaged siding be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be recommended when damage is widespread, materials are deteriorated, moisture has reached the sheathing or matching repairs would not provide a durable and consistent result.

Can siding damage lead to water intrusion?

Yes. Open joints, cracks, missing panels, failed caulking and damaged trim can allow moisture behind the exterior finish and should be evaluated promptly.

Can you repair soffit, fascia and exterior trim with the siding project?

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

Do siding repairs include painting and sealing?

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Do you handle the complete bathroom project or only tile?

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

What should I document after storm or water damage?

Take clear photos and videos of the affected areas, record when the damage was discovered, protect the property from additional damage when safe, and keep receipts. Luna can document the physical repair scope and organize construction information for the claim file.

What is an insurance supplement?

A supplement requests review of repair items, quantities or costs that were missed or insufficient in the original estimate. Strong supplements are supported by measurements, photos, trade pricing, material requirements, invoices and applicable code information.

Can Luna meet the insurance adjuster?

Yes. We can meet at the property to point out visible damage, review measurements and explain the proposed construction scope. We do not decide insurance coverage or act as a public adjuster.

What is recoverable depreciation?

On some replacement-cost claims, part of the estimated amount may be withheld initially as depreciation and may become payable after qualifying repairs are completed and documented. The policy and settlement letter control whether depreciation is recoverable.

What is the difference between ACV and RCV?

Actual Cash Value generally reflects replacement cost after depreciation. Replacement Cost Value generally reflects the estimated cost to replace damaged property with comparable materials, subject to policy terms, limits and deductible.

Can overhead and profit be included?

General contractor overhead and profit may be appropriate when a project requires coordination of multiple trades, scheduling, supervision and project management. Whether it is allowed on a specific claim depends on the repair scope, policy and carrier review.

Who is responsible for the deductible?

The deductible is generally the policyholder's responsibility under the insurance policy. Estimates and invoices should reflect the actual repair cost and should not misrepresent the deductible or completed work.

What documents help support the repair scope?

Helpful records can include photographs, measurements, roof reports, moisture documentation, material specifications, code requirements, equipment information, trade invoices and before-and-after records.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Kitchen Island Layout Tips in McKinney, TX

A useful kitchen island supports traffic, storage and work zones without crowding appliances or door swings.

Kitchen island field-measure checklist

  • Wall-to-wall dimensions and existing cabinet layout
  • Appliance, dishwasher and door swing clearances
  • Primary work paths and seating positions
  • Sink, plumbing, electrical and ventilation requirements
  • Cabinet anchorage, countertop overhang and support details

Test the island at full operating size

Layout should be checked with appliance and cabinet doors open, not only as an empty rectangle on a plan. Exact clearances depend on the room, appliances, seating and applicable requirements, so field measurements come before cabinet ordering.

Plan utilities before finish surfaces

A sink, dishwasher, outlets or specialty appliance can affect plumbing, electrical, ventilation and the floor below. Those routes and inspection steps should be settled before anchoring cabinets or templating countertops.

Coordinate structure and finishes

Countertop material, overhang, seating and cabinet construction determine support needs. Flooring height, end panels, fillers, trim and adjacent walkway finishes should also be part of the scope so the island looks integrated rather than added later.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Do you handle the complete bathroom project or only tile?

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Flooring FAQ

Which flooring works well for busy households?

Luxury vinyl plank and quality porcelain tile are popular for active homes because they provide durable surfaces, practical maintenance and a wide range of styles. The best option also depends on moisture exposure, pets, traffic and the condition of the subfloor.

Do floors need leveling before installation?

Some properties require patching, grinding or leveling so the finished floor lies flat and performs correctly. The existing surface and subfloor should be evaluated before installation begins.

Can damaged flooring be repaired without replacing the entire room?

Sometimes. Individual planks, tiles, transitions or small sections may be replaceable when matching material is available and the surrounding floor is still in good condition.

Can you replace flooring after a water-damage loss?

Yes. After the affected area has been stabilized and properly dried, flooring, underlayment, baseboards and related finishes can be replaced as part of the reconstruction scope.

What is included in a complete flooring installation?

A complete scope may include removal, disposal, subfloor preparation, underlayment, flooring installation, transitions, baseboards or shoe molding, caulking and final cleanup, depending on the project.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Can you work from an insurance roofing estimate?

Yes. We can review the approved construction scope, compare it with visible site conditions and complete the covered roofing repairs or replacement. Coverage decisions remain with the carrier and policyholder.

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Roofing FAQ

How do I know whether my roof needs repair or replacement?

The decision depends on the roof age, extent of damage, active leaks, shingle condition, decking condition and whether a localized repair can provide a durable result.

Can hail damage be present without an active leak?

Yes. Hail can damage shingles, flashing, vents and soft metals before water enters the building, so an inspection is important after a severe storm.

What is normally included in a full roof replacement?

A typical replacement may include tear-off, underlayment, shingles, starter, ridge caps, flashing, pipe boots, ventilation, cleanup and replacement of damaged decking when approved or required.

Siding FAQ

When should damaged siding be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be recommended when damage is widespread, materials are deteriorated, moisture has reached the sheathing or matching repairs would not provide a durable and consistent result.

Can siding damage lead to water intrusion?

Yes. Open joints, cracks, missing panels, failed caulking and damaged trim can allow moisture behind the exterior finish and should be evaluated promptly.

Can you repair soffit, fascia and exterior trim with the siding project?

Yes. Related exterior components can be inspected and included in the same repair scope when they are damaged, deteriorated or contributing to water entry.

Do siding repairs include painting and sealing?

When included in the scope, repaired or replaced areas can be caulked, primed, painted and sealed so the exterior has a finished and weather-resistant result.

Bathroom Remodeling FAQ

How long does a complete bathroom remodel usually take?

The schedule depends on demolition, hidden repairs, plumbing or electrical changes, inspections, waterproofing cure times, tile layout, glass fabrication and material availability. A detailed scope and material plan should be established before construction begins.

Can you convert a bathtub into a walk-in shower?

Yes. A tub-to-shower conversion can include demolition, drain and supply-line adjustments, slope preparation, waterproofing, tile, niches, benches, grab-blocking, fixtures and a framed or frameless glass enclosure.

What waterproofing work is included in a custom tile shower?

The system may include substrate preparation, a shower pan or bonded membrane, sealed corners and penetrations, curb or curbless detailing, flood testing when appropriate, and tile installation over the approved waterproof assembly.

Can the bathroom layout or plumbing locations be changed?

Yes, when site conditions allow. Moving a vanity, toilet, tub or shower may require opening walls or concrete, rerouting supply and drain lines, framing changes, permits and additional repair work.

Do you handle the complete bathroom project or only tile?

Luna General Contractors can coordinate the complete remodel, including demolition, carpentry, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, glass, vanity installation, countertops, drywall, painting, trim and final finish work.

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Fencing FAQ

Can you repair only the damaged section of a fence?

Yes. Partial repairs may be practical when the remaining fence is structurally serviceable, the posts are stable and compatible materials are available.

When should a fence be replaced instead of repaired?

Replacement may be a better option when several posts are failing, rot or storm damage is widespread, the fence is leaning throughout or repeated repairs would not provide a durable result.

Are metal fence posts better than wood posts?

Metal posts are commonly selected for improved resistance to rot and soil moisture. The best choice depends on the design, budget, existing structure and local conditions.

Do you install gates and remove the old fence?

Yes. Single gates, double gates, hardware, demolition, disposal and hauling can be included in the written project scope.

Can a new wood fence be stained or sealed?

Yes. Staining or sealing can help protect the wood and create a more consistent finished appearance after the material has reached the appropriate condition for coating.

Drywall FAQ

Can you match an existing wall or ceiling texture?

Yes. We evaluate the existing finish and use the closest practical application method for orange peel, knockdown, hand texture or smooth-wall repairs. Exact matching can depend on the age and previous paint layers.

Do you repair drywall after plumbing or roof leaks?

Yes. After the leak is corrected and the area is properly dried, damaged drywall and insulation can be removed and replaced, then taped, floated, textured, primed and painted as required by the repair scope.

Can you repair only the damaged section instead of replacing the entire wall?

Often yes. Localized holes, access cuts, cracks and damaged panels can usually be patched or replaced in sections when the surrounding drywall remains sound.

What is included in a complete drywall installation?

A complete scope may include measuring, hanging drywall, corner bead, tape, joint compound, multiple finish coats, sanding, texture, cleanup and preparation for primer and paint.

Do you handle drywall for room additions and whole-home remodels?

Yes. We can coordinate drywall installation and finishing for new walls, ceilings, remodels, additions, commercial spaces and multi-room reconstruction projects.
